cost_method: Staffed-service model: (desks x officers x loaded salary) + (mobile teams x annual cost) + one-off case-management system
eligible_population: Verified caseload not yet established; MIB 2017 estimated 25,000 persons with documentation issues
frequency_or_duration: Loaded annual cost per officer; 15 desks x 3 officers; 8 mobile teams at RM250k per year; RM3m one-off system in Phase 1
basis_and_benchmark: Loaded public-officer cost benchmarked to a Grade 41-44 total employment cost including overheads. Phase 2-3 taper reflects backlog clearance moving to steady-state maintenance.
funding_split_basis: existing 0.20 = JPN adjudication capacity already funded within the Ministry of Home Affairs operating vote; reallocated 0.30 = MITRA community-services grant lines redirected to case management; new 0.50 = the incremental desk, mobile-team and case-system cost. ASSUMPTION pending MOF confirmation (VAL-03, VAL-28).

cost_method: Programme cost = eligible cohort x participation rate x unit cost x years
eligible_population: Approximately 16,000 children aged 4-5 in low-income Indian households (ASM-008 derivation)
frequency_or_duration: Per child per year: fee subsidy RM2,750 + transport RM600 + meals RM850
basis_and_benchmark: Fee subsidy benchmarked to registered preschool fee ranges; net of assistance already received. Phase 1: 16,000 x 0.40 x 4,200 x 2 = RM53.76m. Phase 2: 16,000 x 0.70 x 4,200 x 2 = RM94.08m. Phase 3: 16,000 x 0.80 x 4,200 x 2 = RM107.52m.
funding_split_basis: existing 0.35 = per-place funding already flowing to registered preschool providers for children who would enrol regardless; reallocated 0.15 = MITRA education grants; new 0.50 = incremental subsidy, transport and meals. ASSUMPTION pending MOF and MOE confirmation (VAL-03).

cost_method: Asset-condition model: (schools x audit cost) + (share needing works x average works cost) + (schools x digital facility cost) + coordinator training
eligible_population: 528 SJKT
participation_basis: All schools audited; remediation prioritised by audited risk
frequency_or_duration: Audit RM25k per school (one-off); average safety-critical works RM450k for an assumed 30% of schools; digital facility RM85k per school; coordinator training RM3,500 x 2 per school
recurring_or_one_off: One-off capital with a recurring maintenance tail
basis_and_benchmark: Audit: 528 x RM25k = RM13.200m. Digital: 528 x RM85k = RM44.880m split across Phases 1-2. Remediation: 30% of 528 = 158.4 schools x RM450k = RM71.280m phased 30/40/30. Coordinator training: 528 x 2 x RM3,500 = RM3.696m. Total RM133.056m. existing_share REDUCED from 0.55 to 0.20 so that it reflects ONLY the verified RM50m SJKT maintenance line: per CNF-017 MIB 2.0 claims NO part of the national dilapidated-schools programme, and the earlier 0.55 contradicted that resolution. This raises the new-funding requirement, which is the conservative direction.
funding_split_basis: existing 0.20 = the VERIFIED RM50m annual SJKT maintenance line only. Deliberately excludes the national dilapidated-schools programme per CNF-017. reallocated 0.10 = MITRA equipment grants; new 0.70 = audit, digital layer and incremental safety works. GATING on VAL-11.

cost_method: Multi-faith facility model: (institutions audited x audit cost) + (priority institutions x matched safety works) + compliance and temple or estate-legacy referral advisory
eligible_population: Up to 1,200 participating faith-based and community institutions under the current provisional envelope; this is not a verified multi-faith facility baseline
participation_basis: Voluntary participation with state, institutional and any applicable religious-authority consent; needs-ranked with no fixed allocation by religion
frequency_or_duration: Audit RM12k per institution; matched safety works averaging RM120k for approximately 400 priority institutions, federal share 50%; compliance and referral advisory RM6m over six years
basis_and_benchmark: Current envelope only: audit up to 1,200 institutions x RM12k = RM14.400m; safety works at approximately 400 priority institutions x RM120k x 50% federal share = RM24.000m; compliance and temple or estate-legacy referral advisory = RM6.000m; total RM44.400m. The expanded multi-faith definition does not validate or enlarge these volumes. A Phase 1 facility map must recalculate the eligible population, faith-type distribution, priority caseload, partner capacity and fiscal envelope before formal approval. No fixed allocation by religion is assumed.
funding_split_basis: existing 0.10 = local-authority safety-inspection capacity already funded; reallocated 0.35 = provisional MITRA community-institution grant capacity; new 0.55 = the federal share of matched safety works plus audit. All shares require MOF, state and agency validation. The RM44.400m envelope is a planning cap pending the multi-faith facility map, not a coverage commitment (VAL-13).

cost_method: Per-student service model: cohort x unit cost x years, plus one-off platform
eligible_population: Approximately 20,000 Indian students per SPM cohort (provisional)
participation_basis: All students in participating schools receive profiling; intensive support prioritised by income
frequency_or_duration: RM120 per student profiling and clinic support; RM5m one-off platform in Phase 1
basis_and_benchmark: Cohort size derived from the Indian share of the national SPM cohort and is PROVISIONAL. NOTE, flagged by independent critique: this figure (approximately 20,000 per year) coincides with the annual birth-cohort figure at ASM-008. They are NOT the same population - an SPM cohort is drawn from births some seventeen years earlier, when the Indian population share was higher, and only a subset of any birth cohort sits SPM. The coincidence is unexplained and at least one of the two figures is likely wrong. Both are gating on MOE/DOSM confirmation (VAL-09, VAL-14). Unit cost benchmarked to existing school-based guidance service costs but with no external source, hence Provisional.
funding_split_basis: existing 0.40 = school counselling and career-guidance posts already established in MOE; reallocated 0.10 = MITRA education grants; new 0.50 = incremental profiling, clinics and the platform. ASSUMPTION pending MOE confirmation (VAL-14).

cost_method: Programme cost = enrolees x (stipend + programme support) + apprenticeship incentives
eligible_population: Indian SPM leavers not proceeding to tertiary education
participation_basis: 5,000 enrolees in Phase 1, 10,000 in Phase 2, 15,000 in Phase 3 (30,000 cumulative)
frequency_or_duration: Per enrolee: completion stipend RM500 x 12 months = RM6,000, plus programme support RM2,500. Apprenticeship incentive RM4,000 per placement for 1,000 / 2,000 / 3,000 placements
basis_and_benchmark: Training seats themselves run on existing accredited TVET capacity and are counted in existing_share. Phase 1: 5,000 x 8,500 = RM42.5m + RM4.0m apprenticeships. Phase 2: 10,000 x 8,500 = RM85m + RM8m. Phase 3: 15,000 x 8,500 = RM127.5m + RM12m.
funding_split_basis: existing 0.45 = accredited TVET seat funding and HRD Corp employer levy already committed; reallocated 0.15 = MITRA skills grants; new 0.40 = stipends and apprenticeship incentives, which no existing instrument funds. ASSUMPTION pending MOHR and HRD Corp confirmation (VAL-15).

cost_method: Service and publication model: navigation support plus annual data publication
eligible_population: Qualified Indian applicants to pre-university pathways
participation_basis: Navigation support prioritised by household income
frequency_or_duration: RM250 per supported applicant for approximately 20,000 applicants per phase, plus RM1.0m per phase for data publication and review
basis_and_benchmark: RM250 per supported applicant for approximately 20,000 applicants per phase = RM5.000m, plus RM1.000m per phase for data publication and review = RM6.000m per phase, RM18.000m over three phases. No additional matriculation seats are requested and none are costed.
funding_split_basis: existing 0.50 = MOE and MOHE admissions administration already funded; reallocated 0.10 = MITRA education grants; new 0.40 = navigation support and the published data series. ASSUMPTION (VAL-05).

cost_method: Mentoring and placement network model
eligible_population: Indian graduates within three years of completion
participation_basis: Voluntary participation; mentor supply is the binding constraint
frequency_or_duration: RM800 per mentored graduate for approximately 2,500 graduates per phase, plus network coordination
basis_and_benchmark: RM800 per mentored graduate for approximately 2,500 graduates per phase = RM2.000m, plus RM2.000m per phase network coordination and placement brokerage = RM4.000m per phase across Phases 2-3. Unit cost is a planning assumption; no comparable Malaysian programme cost was located.
funding_split_basis: existing 0.30 = university career-services capacity already funded; reallocated 0.20 = MITRA human-capital grants; new 0.50 = mentoring network coordination. ASSUMPTION (VAL-16).

cost_method: Case-management model: (households / caseload per navigator) x loaded navigator cost x years, plus one-off case system
eligible_population: Low-income Indian households facing two or more concurrent barriers
participation_basis: Capped concurrent service capacity: approximately 18,000 households in Phase 1, 42,000 in Phase 2 and 60,000 in Phase 3, i.e. approximately 26% of the 2014-basis low-income Indian household count of 227,600, or approximately 10% of all Indian households at the Phase 3 peak. Cumulative reach is not specified and will depend on case duration and turnover
frequency_or_duration: Loaded annual cost per navigator; caseload 150 households per navigator; 120 / 280 / 400 navigators; case-management system RM18m phased 12/4/2
basis_and_benchmark: Caseload of 150 benchmarked to intensive case-management practice. Phase 1: 120 x 72k x 2 = RM17.28m + RM12m system. Phase 2: 280 x 72k x 2 = RM40.32m + RM4m. Phase 3: 400 x 72k x 2 = RM57.6m + RM2m. Coverage is deliberately capped and is NOT universal.
funding_split_basis: existing 0.10 = Department of Social Welfare case-work capacity already funded; reallocated 0.40 = MITRA welfare grant lines redirected from episodic aid to case management, the single largest reallocation in the portfolio; new 0.50 = the navigator cadre and case system. ASSUMPTION pending MOF and MITRA confirmation (VAL-28).

cost_method: Enterprise advisory model: enterprises x advisory cost, plus certification and consortium support
eligible_population: Indian-owned microenterprises and small businesses with growth potential
frequency_or_duration: RM6,000 per enterprise structured advisory; plus certification and consortium support of RM6m total
basis_and_benchmark: 5,000 enterprises x RM6,000 structured advisory = RM30.000m, plus RM6.000m certification and consortium support = RM36.000m across Phases 2-3. NO new financing facility is created and none is costed - financing continues on existing TEKUN, SPUMI, AIM and BRIEF-i rails.

cost_method: Matched-savings model: participating households x annual matching cap x years
eligible_population: Low-income Indian households with savings capacity
participation_basis: 15,000 households in Phase 1, 35,000 in Phase 2, 50,000 in Phase 3
frequency_or_duration: Matching capped at RM1,000 per household per year, with the matching ratio varying by income band
basis_and_benchmark: Structured on the MIB 2017 design (pp.41 and 112) of a seed fund providing matching booster units in a qualifying unit-trust or savings product. This is a NEW instrument modelled on an MIB design that was never implemented, not the revival of a lapsed scheme. Requires MOF design approval and, if PNB is the vehicle, PNB's own commercial agreement.
funding_split_basis: existing 0.00 = no existing instrument reaches this population, so nothing can be netted off; reallocated 0.20 = MITRA savings and welfare grants; new 0.80 = the matching contribution. GATING on VAL-19 (PNB participation is a commercial decision Cabinet cannot direct).

cost_method: Access-facilitation model: legacy review + (households x deposit and transaction assistance) + targeted site infrastructure
eligible_population: Estate-displaced and low-income Indian households in housing insecurity
participation_basis: Approximately 6,000 households assisted over six years
frequency_or_duration: Legacy review RM8m; deposit and transaction assistance RM5,000 per household; targeted site infrastructure RM40m over six years
basis_and_benchmark: Housing units themselves are funded through existing national and state housing programmes and are NOT costed here. The Bestari Jaya unit price of RM45,000 is a single-project figure and is expressly NOT used to derive a national unit cost.
funding_split_basis: existing 0.30 = existing affordable-housing and SJKP programme capacity; reallocated 0.10 = MITRA housing grants; new 0.60 = legacy review, deposit assistance and targeted site works. Housing UNITS are not costed here. ASSUMPTION (VAL-20).

cost_method: Outreach and preparation model: campaigns + preparation programmes + annual data publication
eligible_population: Qualified Indian graduates and school leavers eligible for public service entry
participation_basis: Open participation; no adjustment to entry standards
frequency_or_duration: RM350 per candidate through preparation programmes for approximately 8,000 candidates per phase, plus campaign and publication costs
basis_and_benchmark: RM350 per candidate through preparation programmes for approximately 8,000 candidates per phase = RM2.800m, plus RM4.200m per phase campaign, outreach and annual publication costs = RM7.000m per phase. Design follows the JPA-stated cause: the constraint is application volume, not selection outcomes.
funding_split_basis: existing 0.35 = JPA and SPA recruitment administration already funded; reallocated 0.10 = MITRA human-capital grants; new 0.55 = outreach campaigns, preparation programmes and publication. ASSUMPTION (VAL-21).

cost_method: Development-access and monitoring model

participation_basis: Merit-based selection into existing development programmes
frequency_or_duration: Uses existing INTAN and JPA programmes; MIB 2.0 funds outreach, monitoring and publication only
basis_and_benchmark: Almost entirely a transparency and access measure delivered through existing capacity. Requires publication of grade-band composition, which does not currently exist.
funding_split_basis: existing 0.60 = INTAN and JPA development programmes already funded and already open to these officers; reallocated 0.05 = MITRA grants; new 0.35 = outreach and the grade-band publication. ASSUMPTION (VAL-22).

cost_method: Establishment model: secretariat headcount x loaded cost + operating costs
eligible_population: Whole-of-government coordination
frequency_or_duration: 35 secretariat posts at a loaded RM110k each, plus RM2m per year operating costs
basis_and_benchmark: 35 x 110k = RM3.85m per year + RM2m operating = RM5.85m per year = RM11.7m per two-year phase. Benchmarked to comparable delivery units in the Prime Minister's Department.
funding_split_basis: existing 0.10 = existing coordination capacity in the Prime Minister's Department; reallocated 0.45 = MITRA administrative budget; new 0.45 = the incremental 35-post secretariat. GATING on VAL-23 (establishment approval).

cost_method: Evaluation model: baseline survey + dashboard + DPIA + independent evaluations + annual audit and reporting
eligible_population: Programme monitoring and public reporting
frequency_or_duration: Baseline survey RM6m and dashboard RM8m in Phase 1; DPIA RM1m in Phase 1; mid-term evaluation RM4m in Phase 2; final evaluation RM5m in Phase 3; annual audit and reporting RM1.5m per year
basis_and_benchmark: Phase 1: baseline survey RM6.000m + dashboard RM8.000m + DPIA RM1.000m + annual audit/reporting RM1.500m x 2 = RM18.000m. Phase 2: mid-term evaluation RM4.000m + audit/reporting RM3.000m = RM7.000m. Phase 3: final evaluation RM5.000m + audit/reporting RM3.000m = RM8.000m. Total RM33.000m = 2.10% of the central portfolio, below the 3-5% commonly cited for programmes of this type (benchmark itself uncited - see residual limitation).
funding_split_basis: existing 0.10 = National Audit Department capacity already funded; reallocated 0.25 = MITRA monitoring budget; new 0.65 = baseline survey, dashboard, DPIA and independent evaluations. ASSUMPTION pending DOSM agreement (VAL-24).

cost_method: Eligible preschool cohort derivation
eligible_population: Not applicable - this row documents a derivation, not a cost
frequency_or_duration: n/a
basis_and_benchmark: SUPERSEDED DERIVATION, CORRECTED AFTER INDEPENDENT CRITIQUE. The earlier derivation implied a crude birth rate of approximately 8.9 per 1,000, which is materially below Malaysia's national rate, and it applied a HOUSEHOLD income share (39% of Indian households in the bottom 40%) to a CHILD cohort - low-income households are typically larger, so that understates the low-income child share. Both errors are acknowledged. The planning figure of approximately 16,000 children aged 4-5 in low-income Indian households is therefore NOT presented as a derivation: it is an unvalidated planning assumption with a plausible range of 15,000 to 30,000, and PRG-02 is scaled at the LOWER end, which understates rather than overstates the requirement. A DOSM/MOE cohort extract by household income (VAL-09) is a GATING validation item: if the true cohort is at the upper end, PRG-02's central cost could approach RM480m rather than RM255.360m. This is the single largest unquantified exposure in the portfolio.
funding_split_basis: n/a - derivation or rate row, carries no funding

frequency_or_duration: n/a

funding_split_basis: Applied at portfolio level; funded 25% by reallocation and 75% new, consistent with the weighted average of the programme lines it overheads. ASSUMPTION.

frequency_or_duration: n/a
basis_and_benchmark: Conservative = fixed + 0.75 x variable. Central = fixed + 1.00 x variable. Expanded = fixed + 1.30 x variable. Fixed components (systems, audits, secretariat, evaluations) do not scale with participation. Scenarios express participation and unit-cost uncertainty on the SAME programme definitions - they are sensitivity cases, not alternative blueprints.

eligible_population: Applies to the whole model

This UNDERSTATES the nominal cash requirement in Years 3-6; at 2.5% annual inflation the Year 5-6 cash requirement would be approximately 10-13% higher than stated. This is disclosed as a limitation and is a Treasury validation item.

eligible_population: Not applicable - derivation row
frequency_or_duration: n/a
basis_and_benchmark: SSPA Gred 9 (formerly Grade 41/42) basic salary runs approximately RM2,250-RM11,110 per month (SRC-018), i.e. roughly RM27,000-RM133,000 per year BASIC. The loaded annual costs used here - RM90,000 for a documentation officer, RM72,000 for a navigator and RM110,000 for a senior secretariat post - assume basic salary plus fixed allowances, employer pension/EPF contribution, and departmental overheads. The LOADING MULTIPLE ITSELF IS NOT SOURCED and is an assumption; only the underlying salary scale is sourced. This is the reason those rows are classed Benchmarked rather than Confirmed.
